about: A social graph of the people in the diary: say which of them know each other and how closely (on a five-step scale, with an optional note), and put several of them into named, colored groups — a person can be in any number of groups. Shown as a force-directed graph on its own page, opened from a button on the People list (not from the sidebar), with a panel beside it that changes with how many people are selected; and as a short line on each person's profile naming their groups and closest connections. These strings are fetched only once the user enables the plugin, and are merged into the app's main bundle under the `plugins.social-graph.` prefix — a key written here as "title" is referenced in code as plugins.social-graph.title.
tone: Same as the main app: plain, calm, second person, no exclamation marks. This is the user's private picture of their own friends and family, so wording should stay warm and neutral — never rank or judge relationships, never imply a weak tie is a bad one.

social-graph.where: The plugin's own page at /plugins/social-graph (a graph canvas, a toolbar above it, and a side panel), the button opening it in the People list's header (which shows `name`), a line under the contact details on each person's profile, the plugin's row in Settings → Plugins, and its two-screen tour.

keys.name: The plugin's name in the Plugins list in Settings, and the label of the button on the People page that opens it. A short noun phrase.
keys.description: One line under the name in the Plugins list, explaining what enabling it does.
keys.title: Heading of the plugin's own page. Usually identical to `name`.
keys.needPeople: Empty-state title on the page when the People list has fewer than two people.
keys.needPeopleDescription: Under that title: why two are needed. A button to the People list sits below it.
keys.selectPeople: Toolbar button above the graph that opens a searchable list to select people without tapping the graph. A selected count may follow it in brackets.
keys.onlyConnected: Label of a small switch above the graph that hides people with no connections and no groups. Short — it sits on one line beside the button above.
keys.graphLabel: Accessible name of the whole graph drawing, read by screen readers. Describes what the picture is.
keys.groups: Small heading above the list of groups in the side panel, and accessible name of the color legend on the graph.
keys.hint: Shown at the top of the side panel when nobody is selected. Explains, in plain words, the two things a selection is for.
keys.noGroups: Under the Groups heading when no group exists yet.
keys.editGroup: Accessible name of the pencil button beside one group in the list. {{name}} is the group's name.
keys.pairTitle: Panel heading when exactly two people are selected. {{a}} and {{b}} are their names.
keys.selectedCount: Panel heading when three or more people are selected; their names are listed underneath.
keys.connections: Small heading above one person's list of connections, with how many there are. Can be 0.
keys.connectTo: Button that opens a searchable list of people not yet connected to the selected person. Picking one opens the pair, which then asks how close they are.
keys.howClose: Question above the five-step closeness picker for two selected people.
keys.strengthLabel: Accessible name of the five-step closeness picker as a whole.
keys.strength1: The weakest of five closeness steps between two people, shown beside the picker once chosen, as a tooltip, and read by screen readers. Describes the relationship, not a judgement of it.
keys.strength2: The second of five closeness steps.
keys.strength3: The middle step — also what new connections start at when several people are connected at once.
keys.strength4: The fourth of five closeness steps.
keys.strength5: The strongest of five closeness steps.
keys.strengthUnset: Shown beside the picker while the two selected people aren't connected yet; choosing a step connects them.
keys.note: Label above the optional note on a connection. Followed by "(optional)" from the app's own strings.
keys.notePlaceholder: Placeholder inside that note field. A gentle prompt, not an instruction.
keys.disconnect: Button that removes the connection between the two selected people, and the confirm button of the dialog it opens.
keys.disconnectTitle: Title of the confirmation dialog for removing a connection.
keys.disconnectDescription: Body of that dialog. Says what goes and what stays.
keys.allConnected: A disabled button's text when three or more people are selected and every pair among them is already connected.
keys.connectAll: Button connecting every not-yet-connected pair among three or more selected people at the middle step. {{count}} is how many pairs will be created.
keys.groupFull: Error toast when adding people would push a group past its size limit. {{count}} is the limit.
keys.groupName: Label of the group name field (in the edit dialog) and accessible name of the inline field that creates a group.
keys.groupNamePlaceholder: Placeholder inside the inline new-group field: two short example group names. The field is narrow.
keys.newGroup: Small dashed chip that turns into a field for naming a new group containing whoever is selected.
keys.editGroupTitle: Title of the dialog for renaming, recoloring or deleting a group.
keys.groupColor: Label above the row of color swatches in that dialog.
keys.deleteGroup: Button in that dialog that deletes the group.
keys.deleteGroupTitle: Title of the confirmation dialog for deleting a group. {{name}} is its name.
keys.deleteGroupDescription: Body of that dialog. Says the people and their connections are kept.
keys.knows: On a person's profile, the word introducing a short inline list of the people they're connected to, closest first.
keys.openInGraph: Link on a person's profile to the graph page with that person selected.
keys.recordLink: How a connection row is described in the backup import review. {{strength}} arrives already translated, as one of strength1–strength5.
keys.recordGroup: How a group row is described in the backup import review. {{name}} is the group's name.
keys.onboarding.graph.title: Title of the tour's first screen, which shows a sample graph.
keys.onboarding.graph.lede: Under that title: how to read the graph — line thickness and the colored rings.
keys.onboarding.graph.demoFamily: A sample group name in the tour's graph. Only shown as text in the legend if at all.
keys.onboarding.graph.demoWork: A second sample group name in the tour's graph.
keys.onboarding.strength.title: Title of the tour's second screen, which has a working closeness picker.
keys.onboarding.strength.lede: Under that title: how to set closeness, and that a note is possible.
keys.onboarding.strength.previewNote: Small text under the sample picker, saying it is only a preview.
keys.you: The node standing for the diary's owner in the graph, and their name wherever the panel lists them ("You and Ana"). The second-person pronoun, capitalised as a name.
keys.showMe: Label of a small switch above the graph that shows or hides the owner's own node. Short.
keys.zoomIn: Accessible name of the + button in the graph's corner.
keys.zoomOut: Accessible name of the − button in the graph's corner.
keys.fitView: Accessible name of the button that resets zoom and pan so every node fits the canvas again.

languageNotes.en: Reference language; source strings are authored here.
languageNotes.es: Tú, not usted, matching the rest of the app. "Grafo" rather than "gráfico", which would read as a chart.
languageNotes.it: Tu, not Lei, matching the rest of the app.
languageNotes.ja: です・ます, matching the rest of the app. Only the unsuffixed `selectedCount`/`connections`/`connectAll` keys are needed — Japanese has a single plural category.
languageNotes.zh: Simplified Chinese, matching the rest of the app. Only the unsuffixed `selectedCount`/`connections`/`connectAll` keys are needed — Chinese has a single plural category.
